prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1234; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and a neck strain, and the file was opened for review. The claimant is not represented by an attorney, so all contact has been made directly with the claimant.

Entry 2: The driver named on the policy was confirmed as the operator of the insured vehicle at the time of the incident. Police records and witness statements place the claimant inside the vehicle when it was struck.

Entry 3: Photographs supplied by the claimant show damage that corresponds to the described impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main source of visual detail for this loss.

Entry 4: Records show no prior damage to the vehicle and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The reported injury pattern also fits the kind and force of a crash at this speed.

Entry 5: The claimant gave the same account of the collision in each conversation, with no changes in sequence or detail. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back has come to light in the medical history review.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a usual course, with care tapering off as the claimant improved. The treating records are consistent with the reported symptoms and recovery timeline.

Entry 7: Based on the information reviewed to date, the claim is ready for a settlement evaluation. The file will be closed once the final medical bill and repair invoice are received.
